whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Administrator exam?

personas.label: Hands-on practitioners
personas.description: You use Administrator features and want to show that you can apply them to real implementation scenarios.

personas.label: Administrators

personas.description: You want a focused credential to strengthen your Salesforce resume and prepare for administrator roles.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Administrator exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This practice test helps you prepare for ADM-201. Practical Salesforce experience helps because many questions ask you to choose the best setup, design, or troubleshooting step for a situation.
bullets: 68% to pass: aim higher than the minimum before you book.
Scenario questions: choose when to use Configuration & Setup, Object Manager & Fields, or Reports & Dashboards.
Hands-on experience helps: you will be better prepared if you have configured or supported Salesforce in a real org, rather than only memorizing notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Aim for at least 80% on timed practice sets before you book. If you score below that, review the topics with the most questions first. Then retry the questions and explain why each wrong option is wrong.

examFormat.heading: Administrator exam format
examFormat.intro: The Administrator exam is timed. Use these details to plan your pace and practice.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a business need and offer several possible Salesforce solutions. Choose the safest option that is easiest to maintain for the Administrator role.
bestWayToPass: Start with the official exam outline: Match each objective to your notes, Trailhead practice, and topics you need to study.
Focus on important topics: Spend more time on Configuration & Setup, Object Manager & Fields, and Reports & Dashboards, which often appear in difficult scenarios.
Practice with a timer: Use timed question sets to learn when to move on and when to return to a marked question.
Read every explanation: Learn why the correct option fits and why the other options do not.

certificationCard.description: Practice test for the Platform Administrator (ADM-201) exam. Use it to check your readiness and practice in exam-like conditions.

keyConcepts.h2: ADM-201 Practice Test: Key Concepts to Review

blocks.heading: Data Model & Object Relationships
blocks.body: The ADM-201 practice exam covers data modeling. Know how Master-Detail differs from Lookup: Master-Detail supports cascade delete and roll-up summaries, and the child record inherits the parent record’s sharing. A Lookup does not support cascade delete or roll-up summaries, and its records can have separate sharing. External IDs help match records with an outside system and support upsert operations. Schema Builder lets you view and create objects and relationships on a visual canvas. Junction objects create many-to-many relationships. Compound fields, such as Address and Geolocation, store several related values in one field. Expect about 3–5 data model questions in each practice set.

blocks.heading: Security & Access Control
blocks.body: Object-level security controls which records a user can create, read, edit, or delete. Profiles and Permission Sets grant these permissions. Field-level security controls access to each field. Record-level access is controlled by OWD, the Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules, Manual Sharing, and Teams. Follow least privilege: start with limited access and grant more only when needed. Login Hours and Login IP Ranges limit when and where users can sign in. Connected Apps and OAuth control API access. Delegated Administration lets selected non-admin users manage certain user groups. Questions may describe what a user can see and ask which setting to change.

blocks.heading: Automation & Process Logic
blocks.body: Flows are the main tool for most ADM-201 automation questions. Record-Triggered Flows run before or after a record is saved. Screen Flows guide users through a process. Scheduled Flows run at a set time, and Autolaunched Flows are called by other automation. Validation Rules stop a record from saving when it fails a condition. Formula fields calculate values and update automatically; users cannot edit them directly. Roll-Up Summary fields total or count child records on a parent. Default field values fill in fields on new records. Cross-Object Formulas can use fields from parent records: up to five levels through Lookup relationships, and one level through Master-Detail relationships from child to parent.

blocks.heading: Reports & Dashboards for Practice Questions
blocks.body: Questions often ask who can see dashboard data. A standard dashboard uses its Running User’s access, so viewers see data available to that user. Dynamic Dashboards let each viewer see data based on their own access; you can have up to five, and viewers need the “Run Reports” permission. Dashboard components, such as charts, gauges, tables, and metrics, use a source report. Report Schedules can run reports and email the results on a schedule. Custom Report Types set which objects and relationships report builders can use. Bucket fields group report values without creating a formula field.

blocks.heading: AppExchange & Change Management
blocks.body: AppExchange packages are either Managed (made by a provider, protected, and upgradeable) or Unmanaged (source can be edited, with no upgrades). Install packages in a sandbox first and check their requested permissions before installing them in production. Change Sets move metadata between orgs in the same Salesforce environment, such as from a sandbox to production. Developer sandboxes have little data; Developer Pro sandboxes have more storage; Partial Copy sandboxes contain a subset of data; Full sandboxes copy all data. A deployment may follow this path: build in a sandbox, test, then deploy with a Change Set, Metadata API, or Salesforce CLI.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass this ADM-201 practice test
scenarioTips.intro: Use this page as a short mock exam. The questions have the same kind of scenarios, four options, and time pressure as ADM-201. After each attempt, check the difficulty heatmap to find the exam topics that need work. Review the matching key concepts above before trying another set.

blocks.heading: Simulate real exam pacing
blocks.body: Answer a full set in one sitting without **Trailhead**, notes, or search. The exam tests how quickly you can recognize patterns in sharing, Flow versus older automation, and report formats. Practicing without lookups helps you recall these concepts.

blocks.heading: Review every explanation
blocks.body: For each incorrect answer, read the explanation and note why the other options do not fit. ADM-201 may offer similar choices, such as Lookup versus **Master-Detail**, Profile versus Permission Set, or **OWD** versus Sharing Rule. This helps you avoid the same mistake when a question is worded differently.

blocks.heading: Drill weak sections from the heatmap
blocks.body: After two or three attempts, check whether most mistakes come from Automation or Security. If they do, pause the practice questions and study that topic. Then return and check whether your heatmap improves.

blocks.heading: Pair with the full administrator guide
blocks.body: If a topic stays red on the heatmap, use the main Platform Administrator page to review the study plan, exam topic weights, and FAQs. Then return to this practice test to check your progress.

blocks.heading: Book the real exam when scores stabilize
blocks.body: Aim to score well above the practice passing mark on several timed attempts in a row. Consistent scores are a stronger sign of readiness than one high score.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications to Consider
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this certification, common next steps in the admin track or consultant track:

sampleQuestions.question: A sales manager wants to find out which reps logged the most calls this month. Which report type should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Tasks and Events report type includes activities such as calls, meetings, and tasks.
whyWrong: This report type centres on Accounts, not on who logged the activities.
Activity History is a related list on a record, not a report type for comparing reps.
This report type is organised around Accounts rather than the reps' activity counts.

sampleQuestions.question: How many fields can you track in field history on a custom object?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Field history tracking can track up to 20 fields on each object.
whyWrong: The limit is 20 fields per object, not 10.
The limit is 20 fields per object, not 15.
25 is above the limit of 20 fields per object.

sampleQuestions.question: Which permission lets a user transfer records owned by someone else?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Transfer Records permission lets users transfer records they do not own to another user.
whyWrong: Modify All Data is a far broader permission than is needed just to transfer records.
View All Data only allows reading records.
Edit lets a user change records they can access; it does not allow transferring records owned by others.

sampleQuestions.question: A new object should keep records private by default, with access opened only when needed. Which setting defines that starting point?
options: Organization-wide defaults, which set baseline record access
Field-level security, which controls which fields a user can see
Permission sets, which grant extra permissions
Profiles, which set object permissions for users
sampleQuestions.explanation: The object’s OWD establishes baseline record access, such as Private or Public Read/Write. Sharing rules, the role hierarchy, or manual sharing can then extend access.
whyWrong: Field-level security controls fields, not baseline record access.
Permission sets grant permissions to users; they do not set the default record access for an object.
Profiles control object and field permissions, not the default sharing of records.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool should an admin use to update a field when a record is created or edited?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Record-Triggered Flow is Salesforce’s recommended declarative tool for automation that runs when a record changes.
whyWrong: Workflow Rules are a legacy tool; Salesforce recommends Flow for new automation.
Code is not needed when a declarative tool can do the job.
Process Builder is a legacy tool; Salesforce recommends Flow for new automation.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a validation rule do?
options: Assigns records to users or queues based on the criteria that an admin sets
Stops records from saving when they do not meet set conditions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Validation Rules protect data quality by stopping a save when the record does not meet the set conditions.
whyWrong: Assigning records is the job of assignment rules.
Sending emails is the job of email alerts.
Reports are built in Report Builder.

sampleQuestions.question: Which report format displays records in rows and columns, like a spreadsheet?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tabular reports list records in rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet.
whyWrong: A summary report groups rows and shows subtotals.
A matrix report groups by both rows and columns.
A joined report combines several report blocks.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a roll-up summary field do?
options: Tracks the history of changes made to fields on the parent record
Totals or counts child records on a Master-Detail parent
sampleQuestions.explanation: Roll-up summary fields can calculate values such as SUM, COUNT, MIN, and MAX from child records on a Master-Detail parent.
whyWrong: Formula fields calculate values from fields on the same or a parent record.
Field history tracking records changes to fields.
Relationship fields link objects.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature controls access to specific fields, even when a user can access the record?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Field-Level Security controls whether users can view or edit fields. Admins set it in Profiles or Permission Sets.
whyWrong: Organization-wide defaults set baseline record access, not field access.
The role hierarchy opens up record access, not field access.
Sharing rules extend record access, not field access.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Master-Detail relationship support that a Lookup relationship does not?
options: Cascade delete, but no roll-up summaries
Cascade delete and roll-up summary fields
Roll-up summary fields, but no cascade delete
sampleQuestions.explanation: Master-Detail supports cascade delete and roll-up summary fields. Lookup relationships are more flexible but do not support these features.
whyWrong: Master-Detail also supports roll-up summary fields.
Master-Detail adds both cascade delete and roll-up summary fields.
Master-Detail also supports cascade delete.

sampleQuestions.question: Which dashboard component displays one value, such as the total sales pipeline?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Metric component highlights one key measure or total.
whyWrong: A gauge shows a value against a target range.
A bar chart compares values across groups.
A table lists rows of data.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use a record type?
options: To trigger a different set of automation rules each time a user edits a record in the object
To assign a page layout, and nothing else
To offer different picklist values, page layouts, and business processes for the same object
To control which records users can see
sampleQuestions.explanation: Record types let you provide different picklist values, page layouts, and business processes for an object.
whyWrong: Record types do not trigger automation.
Page layouts are one part of what a record type controls, not all of it.
Record access is controlled by sharing, not by record types.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature can detect or prevent duplicate accounts or contacts?
options: Validation Rules with a custom error message
sampleQuestions.explanation: Matching Rules identify possible duplicates. Duplicate Rules can then block them or warn users.
whyWrong: Workflow Rules automate actions; they do not compare records.
Validation Rules check one record's values; they do not find matching records.
Process Builder automates actions; it does not detect duplicates.

sampleQuestions.question: What can you customize with Lightning App Builder?
options: Dashboards and their source reports, using a drag-and-drop chart editor
App, record, and home pages using drag-and-drop components
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lightning App Builder lets admins arrange declarative components on app, record, and home pages.
whyWrong: Dashboards are built in the dashboard editor.
Reports are built in Report Builder.
List views are configured on the object tab.

sampleQuestions.question: Which option can share records owned by users in a role or group?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing Rules can grant record access based on ownership, such as sharing records with a role or group.
whyWrong: Manual sharing shares one record at a time.
Organization-wide defaults set the baseline; they do not share records owned by a role or group.
A public group is a set of users that a sharing rule can use; it does not share records by itself.
